source.publication: 2025 Form CT-1040 Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and Form CT-1040
source.section: PDF pages 24-25, Pension and Annuity Worksheet Lines 1-4 and Phase-Out Table (MFJ, 110,000-114,999: .55); PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 70,000.00 + public pension (CT) 40,000.00 = 110,000.00. Federal taxable income = 110,000.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction - 1 x 1,600.00 age 65+ = 76,900.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 110,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 110,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 48b pension and annuity (Line 5b part): Phase-Out Table: federal AGI 110,000.00 is 110,000.00 or more, decimal 0.55; 40,000.00 x 0.55 = 22,000.00 -> 22,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 22,000.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 22,000.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 110,000.00 - 22,000.00 = 88,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 88,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 88,000.00 is more than 71,000.00, exemption 0.00; Line 3 taxable income = 88,000.00 - 0.00 = 88,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Married Filing Jointly/Qualifying Surviving Spouse schedule) on 88,000.00: 20,000.00 x 0.02 + 68,000.00 x 0.045 = 400.00 + 3,060.00 = 3,460.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 88,000.00 is not more than 100,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 210,000.00); Line 7 = 3,460.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.10 (Connecticut AGI 88,000.00 is in the band more than 52,000.00); Line 9 = 3,460.00 x 0.10 = 346.00. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 3,460.00 - 346.00 = 3,114.00 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: Connecticut state employee pension (not a teachers' pension).
